# kcore_ingress_route (Resource)

Ingress route (kind: IngressRoute): hostnames and paths mapped to VM, container, or external backends on a gateway, with load balancing, health checks and per-route WAF settings. Switching a route to WAF block mode after reading the events stays a kctl ingress waf set-mode operation, or edit spec.

See the gateway page for a complete example with a policy, a gateway, and a route.

`gateway` is its own attribute so Terraform creates the gateway first and deletes it last. The provider adds it to the spec it sends; leave `gateway` out of `spec`, or make it equal. Apply plans the route first and stops on validation errors such as a backend VM that does not exist.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `gateway` (String) Name of the gateway that serves the route. Reference `kcore_ingress_gateway.<name>.name` so Terraform creates the gateway first and deletes it last.
- `name` (String) Route name (`metadata.name`).
- `spec` (String) The `spec` of an IngressRoute as JSON, without `gateway`: `hosts`, `paths`, `waf`, `headers`, `redirectHttp`, and for TCP routes `kind` and `port`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait until the route reports ready before apply returns. Certificates are issued by the gateway, so a route with a new hostname can take a few minutes.

### Read-Only

- `certificates` (List of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--certificates))
- `generation` (Number)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `phase` (String) pending, ready, or degraded.
- `status_message` (String)
- `upstreams` (List of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--upstreams))
